title: Applying for a job
subtitle: openings, prospects, cover letter, hands-on
summary: Read job ads and write a cover letter in natural business English, using collocations like career prospects, benefits package, hands-on experience and team player.

lesson.heading: Reading a job ad
lesson.text: A job ad describes the ideal candidate. It may ask whether you have a **genuine passion for** the work - whether you like it very much - and whether you want a **challenging** role, a positive word for something exciting and difficult, in a **fast-paced** environment, one where things happen quickly.

examples.text: Do you have excellent communication skills and a genuine **passion for** customer service?
Are you looking for a **challenging** role within a **fast-paced** working environment?
FDR Bank has several new **openings** for Customer Service Assistants.

lesson.heading: Four other words for 'job' in an ad
rows: Are you looking for a challenging **role**?
my application for the **position** of Customer Service Assistant
lesson.note: All four are more formal than job and are very common in advertisements.

lesson.heading: Who you work for, and what you get
lesson.text: If you **report to** someone, he or she is your boss. A good ad promises **full training** (all the training you need), a **competitive salary** (as good as, or better than, other salaries for similar jobs) and an **attractive benefits package** - all the extra benefits a company offers as well as a salary.

examples.text: **Reporting to** the Customer Service Manager, you will deal with customer enquiries.
No previous **experience** is necessary as **full training** will be given.
We offer a **competitive salary** and an attractive **benefits package** including pension, healthcare plan and **subsidised** meals.
examples.note: subsidised = partly paid for by the company

lesson.heading: Getting on in the company
lesson.text: A good **post** offers excellent **career prospects** - opportunities for promotion and career development - to candidates who **demonstrate leadership qualities**, the ability to lead a group. You then **fill in an online application form**, giving details of your **salary expectations**.

examples.text: The post offers excellent **career prospects** to candidates who demonstrate **leadership qualities**.
We are keen to **promote and develop talent** within the company.
Click here to **fill in the online application form**, including details of your **salary expectations**.

lesson.heading: The cover letter
lesson.text: You want your application to **stand out** - to be better than the others - so include a clear **cover letter** (also called a **covering letter**) which highlights key points from your CV. If you do not know the name of the reader, begin **Dear Sir or Madam** and end **Yours faithfully**.

examples.text: Please find attached my CV **in support of** my application for the **position of** Customer Service Assistant.
Specify the job you are applying for at the beginning of the letter.
Thank you for taking the time to consider this application and I look forward to hearing from you.

lesson.note: Mention any studies or training courses that are relevant to the role, and any relevant experience, to show your suitability for the role.

lesson.heading: Describing your own experience
lesson.text: Say you are keen to gain **hands-on experience** - practical, direct experience rather than theoretical knowledge - in this **field**, meaning this area of business or activity. **Customer-facing** work means dealing directly with customers. A **team player** is a person who is good at working with others.

examples.text: I have just completed my degree in Business Studies and am keen to gain **hands-on** experience in this area.
I have always been interested in working in this **field**.
This has given me valuable **customer-facing** experience, as well as developing good communication skills.
I am a **team player** and I am keen to develop my career and gain **managerial experience** in the future.
examples.note: managerial experience = experience of managing other people

lesson.heading: Useful collocations from the ad and the letter
rows: company scheme that pays for medical treatment
as good as or better than salaries for similar jobs
ability to explain and listen well
the form you fill in on a website
be in charge of a group of people
do a piece of work from start to finish

lesson.text: If you do not know the reader's name, Dear Sir or Madam goes with Yours faithfully - never with Yours sincerely.

exercises.prompt: Match the two parts of these business collocations.
Match these words to complete four more collocations from the unit.
You don't need to have done this job before - no ___ is necessary.
exercises.hint: (two words: experience of this type of job from before)
exercises.explanation: Ads often say no previous experience is necessary when full training will be given.

exercises.prompt: As part of my new job, I get ___ meals - the company pays part of the cost.
exercises.explanation: Something subsidised is partly paid for by the company.

exercises.prompt: It's really important to make your application ___ from all the others.
exercises.explanation: To stand out is to be noticeably better than the rest.

exercises.prompt: Working in the factory over the summer gave me some ___ experience of manufacturing.
exercises.explanation: Hands-on experience is practical, direct experience.

exercises.prompt: I'm hoping to work in the ___ of automotive manufacturing.
exercises.explanation: A field is an area of business or activity.

exercises.prompt: The ad said the company will provide all the training you need, so ___ will be given.
exercises.explanation: Full training means all the training you need to do the job.

exercises.prompt: You should only apply for the job if you have ___ experience.
exercises.explanation: Managerial experience is experience of managing other people, for example leading a team.

exercises.prompt: The salary isn't great, but they offer an attractive ___.
exercises.explanation: A benefits package is all the extras a company offers as well as a salary.

exercises.prompt: I am sending my CV in ___ of my application for the position of sales team leader.
exercises.explanation: The fixed phrase is in support of my application.
You have a passion for something.

exercises.prompt: Jakob's experience is more relevant ___ the job than Sylvana's.
exercises.explanation: Something is relevant to a job or a role.

exercises.prompt: In my previous role ___ Sales Representative, I reported to the Sales Manager.
exercises.explanation: In my previous role as (job title) - and you report to your boss.

exercises.prompt: He only has 6 months' experience as a trainee. I don't think that makes him ___ for the job of quality manager.
exercises.explanation: Someone is suitable for a job; the noun is suitability.

exercises.prompt: What do we call a job which deals directly with the customers?
exercises.explanation: Customer-facing work means dealing directly with customers.

exercises.prompt: How can we describe a working environment which is busy and rapidly changing?
exercises.explanation: In a fast-paced environment, things happen quickly.

exercises.statement: If you report to the Customer Service Manager, that person is your boss.
exercises.explanation: Correct - to report to someone means that he or she is your boss.

exercises.statement: A letter that begins Dear Sir or Madam should end Yours sincerely.
exercises.explanation: It should end Yours faithfully. Yours sincerely goes with a named person.

exercises.prompt: Does each item describe what the company offers, or what the candidate offers?
Put this opening line of a cover letter in order.
exercises.answer: Please find attached my CV in support of my application
exercises.explanation: Specify the job you are applying for right at the beginning of the letter.
